ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 65:35 ratio of high-intensity white pixels to low-intensity black/shadowed pixels across the visible ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white regions occupy the distal two-thirds of both lobes. A central dark-pigmented region forms an inverted triangle extending from the peduncle to the median notch. Secondary black mottling and focal spotting are concentrated along the trailing edges and transition zones.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with an internal angle of approximately 55 degrees; depth relative to lobe height is approximately 15 percent.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations are present along the entire trailing edge of both lobes. The right lobe exhibits several larger-amplitude valleys (approx. 10-20 pixels deep) creating a jagged profile.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Outer margins display a consistent convex curvature tapering toward sharp distal tips. The trailing edges follow a shallow sigmoid curve from the tips toward the central notch.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple circular, high-contrast white clusters (approx. 3-8 pixels in diameter) are visible on the dark central pigmentation, particularly near the peduncle and lower central lobe areas.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several faint, unaligned light-gray linear markings (rake marks) are detected traversing the dark central pigment on a vertical and diagonal axis.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Pronounced irregular tissue loss or jagged wear pattern along the trailing edge of the right lobe; presence of numerous white punctate scars likely from barnacle attachment sites.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique 'dripping' pattern of dark pigment spots extending into the white fields from the distal trailing edges, most notably on the right lobe tip.
